counter_probe_anchor_falsifier.finding: The product's counter-authority stage anchors every issued probe on the first four key terms of the ANSWER PROSE (product/query/adversarial_retrieval.py::plan_adversarial_queries, `probe_terms = key_terms[:4] + terms`), and the generative audit rewrites that prose first, replacing every ungrounded citation with the literal placeholder '[citation removed: not in retrieved set]'. The placeholder's own tokens survive the product's own stoplist and length filter ('citation', 'removed', 'retrieved'), so when the answer carries enough placeholder occurrences they displace the real legal vocabulary out of the four anchor slots. In the German bundle of packet 39319405429 the issued probe reads 'citation removed retrieved nicht ...' and the anchor shares NO content term with the question it is supposed to attack; in the German bundle of packet 39275520116 three of the four anchor slots are placeholder tokens. The FR and IT bundles of the same packets are clean, so the defect is not a language artefact. The de-redaction counterfactual isolates the placeholder as the cause: removing ONLY the placeholder occurrences from the answer prose changes the anchor to 'nicht fuer... ' / 'fuer... arbeitgeber ...' and restores a topical anchor, while for every bundle without a placeholder the de-redaction is a no-op. All five non-vacuity controls pass, including byte-for-byte replay of every recorded probe query by the product's own planner (14/14).
